title: Block C close: the middle of the book
hookLine: poets, ants, spiders, queens, and the command to know one another

lines: POETS, AN ANT, A HOOPOE, A QUEEN.
cards: Poets wandering in every valley. An ant warning her colony. A hoopoe with news, a queen on a throne, a spider's house, a sea of ink, a man running from the city's edge.
Seventy-six days ago this path opened Surah Ash-Shu'ara, the Poets, and since then it has read through twenty-five surahs, from the twenty-sixth to the fiftieth. Today, Block C closes.
Before turning toward the last part of the book, it's worth standing still in the middle and looking both ways.

teach.b: The Qur'an has been divided, for reciting, into thirty roughly equal parts, each called a juz'. Some Muslims read one juz' a day in Ramadan and finish the whole book in a month.
Block C began in the nineteenth juz' and ended in the twenty-sixth: the middle stretch, the long walk between the great opening surahs and the short, bright ones at the end. Look at what lived here.

teach.h: STORIES: A MOTHER, AN ANT, A QUEEN.
teach.b: Stories: Musa's mother, her heart emptied with fear, setting her baby on the river. Sulayman smiling at an ant. The Queen of Sheba stepping onto a floor she thought was water.
Ayyub striking the ground and finding a spring. The believer in Pharaoh's house who spoke up. Then wisdom: Luqman's advice to his son, walk modestly and lower your voice.
If the sea were ink, the words of Allah would not run out.
Don't despair of mercy. Repel evil with what is better.

And in the last stretch, a manual for living together: consult one another, fatabayyanu, islah, no mocking, no backbiting, and the verse addressed to all humanity: We made you nations and tribes, taqwa.
And Qaf: the reminder underneath it all. A middle is easy to rush on the way to an ending. This one held a great deal: story, wisdom, life together, and nearness.

how: The Qur'an is often read in thirty parts, one juz' a day, especially in Ramadan, and printed copies mark each juz' and its halves and quarters in the margins.

o: a single verse within a longer surah
one of the Qur'an's chapters, a surah
one of thirty equal parts of the Qur'an

games.q: Block C, the middle of the book — tap the pairs.
p: nations and tribes, to know one another

s: from Ash-Shu'ara, the Poets, to Qaf.
a juz' is one of thirty roughly equal parts; it can hold many surahs or part of one.
the sea of ink verse says Allah's words would run out
it says the words of Allah would not run out, even with the sea and more seas as ink.

games.q: you want to finish the whole Qur'an in Ramadan. how is it often divided?
o: one juz' a day, thirty parts in thirty days.
the first and last surahs only.
games.why: the book is divided into thirty juz' for exactly this kind of daily reading.

practice: Let the last seventy-six days run past like a road seen from a train: the poets, the ant, the spider, the sea of ink, Ya-Sin, the forgiver, the kneeling, the jinn, the opening at Hudaybiyyah, the private rooms, the jugular.
Don't choose too fast; wait for the verse that comes back on its own. When it comes, say it to yourself slowly, twice, and if you pray, thank Allah for it.
